title: The title over the cross proclaims Christ king
english: And they placed above his head the written charge against him: This is Jesus, the king of the Jews (Matthew 27:37). Whether by occasion or by truth, Christ is proclaimed king, and every letter bears witness to his reign—whether Greek, Roman, or Hebrew. No other ground for his death is found except this: he was king of the Jews. But I have been appointed king by him over Zion (Psalm 2:6).
translator_notes: PG 13 Latin Series CLOSEOUT arc; no Heine.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Origen is beginning his commentary on Matthew, treating the crucifixion scene where the soldiers place the written charge over Jesus' head.

title: The bribed soldiers' false report
english: They gathered with the elders and took counsel to give money to the soldiers, so that they would say, “His disciples stole him during the night while we were sleeping.” Those who were reading “You shall not bear false witness” (Exodus 20:16) were inviting others to bear false witness. Glory to the risen Christ. Amen.
translator_notes: Series CLOSEOUT tip — passion/resurrection end of Commentariorum Series in PG 13 before Luke Homilies.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Matthew 27:62-66, where the chief priests and elders bribe the soldiers to say that Jesus' disciples stole his body while they slept.
